summary: Friedrich Windischmann studied Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies at Bonn and Munich under Lassen, Schlegel, and others. He taught canon law and New Testament exegesis at Freising and Munich, and served as Generalvikar in Munich (1846–1861).

A linguist who studied at Rostock and Leipzig under Gottfried Hermann and Moriz Haupt, Friedrich Zarncke founded the Literarisches Centralblatt für Deutschland in 1850. He served as privatdozent and later Rektor (1869–1882) at the University of Leipzig.

Friedrich von Adelung worked in Indology, linguistics, and archaeology after studying at Leipzig (1787–1790). He became director of the School of Oriental Languages in Saint Petersburg in 1824 and held positions in Vienna, Kharkiv, Tartu, and Utrecht.

Friedrich von Spiegel specialized in Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies, earning his PhD at Jena (1842) after studies at Erlangen, Bonn, and Leipzig. He was Professor of Oriental Languages at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg from 1849 to 1891.

Frits Staal was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and linguistics who studied at Amsterdam, Madras, and Banaras Hindu University. He held professorships at the University of Amsterdam (1962–1967) and the University of California, Berkeley (1968–1991).

Fritz Burg, who worked in Indology and related fields, earned his Ph.D. from Humboldt University of Berlin (1881–1885). He spent his career at the Hamburg State and University Library, serving as a librarian from 1907 to 1926.

Specializing in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics, Fritz Georg Wolff studied at Munich, Heidelberg under Hermann Osthoff, Berlin, and Giessen, where he completed his Ph.D. under Christian Bartholomae (1903–1905).

Linguist and historian Fritz Hommel studied at Leipzig under Friedrich Delitzsch and Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer (1874–1877), and at Munich. He then held an academic post at the University of Munich from around 1877 to 1925.

Indologist Fritz Johaentgen studied at Bonn under Christian Lassen and Martin Haug, and completed his Ph.D. at Berlin under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber. He served as a Privatdozent at Humboldt University of Berlin from 1864 to 1878.

Fritz Kern, a historian and Indologist, studied at Lausanne, Tübingen, and Berlin, where he completed his Ph.D. He held posts at Kiel, was ordinary professor at Frankfurt (1914–1922), and served as professor at Bonn (1925–1947).

Philosopher Fritz-Joachim von Rintelen completed his studies and habilitation at Munich. He held professorships at Bonn (1934), Munich (1936–1941), and Mainz (1947–1969), alongside guest professorships at Córdoba, UCLA, Tokyo, and Chicago.

Frédéric Baudry, a scholar of linguistics and Indology, studied at the École Normale Supérieure and under Eugène Burnouf. He worked as a librarian at Versailles and the Bibliothèque de l'Arsenal before directing the Bibliothèque Mazarine (1874–1885).

Frédéric Richard specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He earned a BA at the University of Lausanne and trained at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute, later working at Lausanne and the Centre intercantonal d'information sur les croyances.

Frédéric-Guillaume Bergmann studied linguistics and Indology at Strasbourg, Paris, Göttingen, and Berlin. He spent his career at the University of Strasbourg, directing the foreign literature course in 1838 and serving as professor from 1840 to 1877.

Frédéric-Gustave Eichhoff was a linguist and Indologist who received his Ph.D. from the University of Paris. He taught at the Sorbonne and served as professor of foreign literature at the University of Lyon from 1842 to 1855.
Fu Yan was a scholar of philosophy and Sinology who studied at the Royal Naval College from 1877 to 1879. He later held posts at Fudan University (1905–1906) and Peking University (1912).

Fu-shih Lin was a Sinologist and historian of religion who completed graduate studies at Princeton under Ying-shih Yü, Denis Twitchett, and Stephen F. Teiser. He held a post at Academia Sinica from 1994 until 2021.
Fuguan Xu was a scholar of Sinology, philosophy, and history who studied at Meiji University and under Shili Xiong. He held an academic post at Tunghai University from around 1955 to 1969.

Fuhui Zhang works in linguistics, Tibetology, and history. He served as a professor at Northeast Normal University (2004) and earned his PhD in applied linguistics there (2013–2018), with an affiliation attested at Tianshui Normal University in 2012.

Fujio Oda is an archaeologist and historian who studied at Kyushu University from 1952 to 1956. He held academic posts at Beppu University from around 1969 to 1985 and at Fukuoka University from around 1985 to 2004.
